content: The initiation of enteral feeding within the first few days of life is recognized to influence the development of unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. However, the impact of early intravenous nutrition on the occurrence of neonatal jaundice has not been established. The objective of this review was to evaluate the effect of early intravenous nutrition on neonatal jaundice. To achieve this, the Cochrane Neonatal Review Group's standard search strategy was employed. This included a comprehensive search of the Cochrane Controlled Trials Register (Cochrane Library: Issue 3, 2002), MEDLINE (spanning 1966 to December 2002), and EMBASE (spanning 1974 to December 2002). The inclusion criteria were randomized or quasi-randomized controlled trials that assessed the effect of early intravenous nutrition on levels of unconjugated bilirubin. Despite the extensive search, no studies meeting the inclusion criteria were identified. Consequently, no data were available for analysis. In conclusion, there is no evidence from randomized or quasi-randomized controlled trials to determine the effect of early intravenous nutrition on neonatal jaundice. Therefore, decisions regarding the initiation of early intravenous nutrition should continue to be guided by considerations other than its potential impact on neonatal jaundice.
